Content:
1- Camera's are performing a bit better than Oneplus13 even with the downgraded hardware.
2- Processor chip is stronger now than before
3- Its back has extraordinary durability, only a diamond can put a scratch on it, moreover it is ip66/68/69/69k rated  now.
4- It has additional wifi chip in it, you won't drop signals and consistency will remain unlike other flagships.
5- It has newer touch sampling chip as well which makes user experience great and it matters for people who play games on mobile phones.
6- It has 165 hz now and it matters for gamers. However it gets activated only during gaming. During normal use, it switches between 1 and 120 only not 30,60,90 etc so yeah it makes user experience good.
7- Oxygen OS 16 is highly customizable and really good to use and this mindspace thing is actually nice and useful.
Yeah, im a bit disappointed too because of camera's, it should be comparable to other flagships but it is not. Oneplus lags behind in camera but ig since they're associated with OPPO so their focus is now on performance/user experience side, while OPPO's focus is on camera and other stuff too like other flagships. Oneplus 15 Camera's are still good enough for daily use tbh but not at the level of other top flagships. If you want really good user experience, performance, customization, massive battery and somewhat above average camera then this is for you. If you want true high end camera's then but can compromise on some other things then you can for other brands. OxygenOS is really fun to use and remember, Iphone and samsung and pixel too still doesn't offer ip69 rating and Iphone's this year build is technically trash, can be easily scratched. Samsung is good and will always be a decent choice, pixel is good but trash at the same time since it lacks behind in literally every department except the cameras and OS. So yeah, think what you actually want from a cell phone and choose accordingly.

Correct me if I am wrong and missed something except the 1.5k resolution which really doesn't make much difference.

Author: @techstar796
Content:
I feel like Oppo and OnePlus are now trying to separate their identities. Oppo is becoming more camera centric 📸 and OnePlus is moving towards a gaming centric direction 🎮. But this is not the OnePlus we all knew before. OnePlus used to be the real flagship killer, the brand people trusted when there weren’t strong competitors between Samsung and Apple. It created a huge impact in smartphone history.

Now I’m honestly disappointed with the direction OnePlus is taking. Gaming is not the main priority for everyone. If they really wanted to target gamers, they could have done it under the Nord series with something like a Nord GT. They could have still kept the main OnePlus lineup as the flagship killer it once was.

Since the UI is almost the same as Oppo with only small differences, many people will naturally shift to Oppo. And if someone wants the best camera performance with this UI, the Oppo Find X9 Ultra or Pro would be the best choice 📷🔥. I think Oppo will now get the brand value that OnePlus once enjoyed.

I really appreciate Vivo and iQOO for what they are doing 🙌. They even moved from Funtouch OS to Origin OS, and now people will finally trust them more in terms of software. Let’s see what happens, but I don’t think OnePlus will capture much of the market anymore except among gamers.

Vivo will probably do much better because of this shift from OnePlus. And even the Oppo Find X series, which never got enough attention before, will now start getting the recognition it deserves ⭐.

This is my point based on my knowledge, and I genuinely feel this is what’s going to happen.

Author: @HeiiKun
Content: Really wish you'd start using Wh instead of mAh for battery size. The OP15 actually has a 7.56v 3650mAh battery (27.6Wh). The 7300mAh is a fake rating assuming the dual cell battery was put in parallel instead of series. I've also seen phones list their actual mAh while having a 3.9v silicon-carbon battery, making them undersell their battery capacity. mAh is actually just a terrible way to depict power. It's like trying to measure the circumference of the earth using football fields, but using the median length of all the fields that exist in the closest country to a point on the measured circumference. Meaning if you're measuring somewhere in America it'll be X length, somewhere in Africa will be Y length, somewhere in Asia will be Z length, etc. Seems pretty confusing to measure the circumference of the earth in something that varies length doesnt it?

Content:
@oneplus_india @oneplus @petelau

Subject: Feature Request – Call End Tone via Earbuds & Power Button Behavior on Incoming Calls (OnePlus 12 / 13s)
Dear OnePlus Team,
I’m a OnePlus 12  and 13s user and I’d like to highlight two important usability features that were available in earlier OnePlus devices (like the OnePlus 6), but are currently missing in newer models like the OnePlus 12 and 13R. These small enhancements can make a significant difference in user experience.
1. Call End Beep Sound via Earbuds or Bluetooth:
When using earbuds or a Bluetooth headset during a call, there's no tone or audio feedback when the call ends.
This feature existed on older OnePlus devices like the OnePlus 6. And Samsung galaxy s24, galaxy flip 7.
Samsung phones currently offer this functionality with a "call end tone".
It’s especially useful when the phone is in a pocket, bag, or placed away — users don't realize when the call has ended.
Request: Please consider reintroducing the Call End Beep Tone (for Bluetooth/Earbud calls) feature in OxygenOS.
2. Power Button Function During Incoming Calls:
When a call is ringing and the phone is on a table, pressing the power button immediately rejects the call, instead of simply turning off the screen.
On the OnePlus 6 and Samsung galaxy s24 and Samsung flip 7, pressing the power button would just turn off the screen without disconnecting or rejecting the call.
Samsung phones also behave similarly.
This is especially useful during meetings, religious settings, or other quiet environments where one may want to silence the phone without rejecting the call.
Request: Please consider adding a toggle option in OxygenOS for:
“Press Power Button to Turn Off Screen Only (Don’t End or Reject Call)”
Thank you for continuing to build reliable, user-friendly devices. Bringing back these small, thoughtful features can further enhance the overall OnePlus experience.
Kind regards,
[Ashitosh]
OnePlus 12, oneplus 13s User, maharashtra, India

I used to be a huge OnePlus fan. I bought the OnePlus X, then the 3, 5, 6, 8 Pro, and 9 Pro all on launch day. But the 9 Pro overheated so badly that I finally gave up and moved to an iPhone 13. Since then I’ve gone pretty deep into the ecosystem: my mom and wife use iPhones, I’ve moved through the 15 Plus and now the 17, and I’m using AirPods Pro, a MacBook Air, and an Apple Watch Series 7 and now 11.

Maybe someday Apple will annoy me enough to switch back, but it’s unlikely. They’d have to disappoint me across multiple product lines for that to happen. That’s the tough reality: with Android you can switch brands any time, but escaping Apple’s ecosystem once you’re in it is much harder.

Content: I got the OnePlus 13 this year and its has been good but not great. The main problem I have is with Wifi 6 connectivity, on many networks the connection just cuts out and I have to turn off and on Wifi to get internet again. Maybe them changing the modem has something to do with this, but maybe it still doesn't support multi ban steering, I kinda don't want to take the risk. Does anyone else have this problem on the 13? The rest of the 13 is great but everything I care about got upgraded on the 15, performance and battery, lower screen res for better battery, cheaper cameras are fine cause I don't care about them. Only thing lost is the easier to use alert slider, and I have the 13 without the glass back so its less prone to breaking. Honestly the 13 was a good value when I got it and a good upgrade from my OP6, but I I'm going to consider biting the bullet and getting the next Xperia when they re-design it, hopefully with the new battery technology and Qi2.
